findings.finding: Claim under doubt: scenario.ts rule 2b's isProvablyNewerRunId check plus association.ts's supersedeMissionContext together make the persisted association monotonic (never regresses) — Two overlapping polls can compute different 'newer than R1' targets (R2 vs R3) from the same stale snapshot; the faster one writes R3 first, then the slower one overwrites it back down to R2 because supersedeMissionContext only checked 'source is transcript_run_id and value differs from current', never true compare-and-set against the decision's own basis.
findings.suggestion: Re-validate against the store's CURRENT missionContext at write time using the exact value the caller's decision was based on (compare-and-set), not a fresh re-read; or a rebuttal showing this interleaving cannot occur in practice.

findings.finding: The “content-fingerprinted” supersession memo is not actually a content fingerprint: it uses only transcript length and the final 256 characters. Distinct bounded transcript snapshots can have the same length and suffix while containing a different later corroborated `Run-ID:` footer earlier in the tail. In that case `buildRecoveryThunk` replays a previously recovered run without re-scanning, so the Mission context can remain on the wrong run and fail the stale-association recovery behavior.
findings.suggestion: Use a collision-resistant fingerprint of the complete transcript snapshot (for example a hash), or include a reliable transcript revision/offset supplied by the reader. Do not reuse a recovery result based only on length plus a short suffix.

findings.finding: supersedeMissionContext` overwrites whichever association is currently stored, without checking that it is still the stale association from which the resolver made its decision. A concurrent request can update the task association after resolution (for example, from a newer live pointer), and this delayed supersession can then overwrite that newer association with an older transcript-derived result.
findings.suggestion: Pass the expected previous association into `supersedeMissionContext` and compare its run ID and `observedAt` before patching. If it no longer matches, skip the write and let the next resolve operate on the current association.

findings.finding: The timestamp UI tests validate relative-time text and absence, but do not validate the required full-date tooltip. Removing the `title={new Date(at).toLocaleString()}` behavior from `FeedTime` would still leave all newly added client timestamp tests passing.
findings.suggestion: Assert that a timestamped card’s `.mc-feed-time` element has a non-empty `title` representing the event timestamp, preferably with a deterministic locale/time-zone setup.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The four requested behaviors are substantially implemented and covered, but the supersession cache can return stale run identity for distinct transcript content, and the association update needs a compare-before-write guard to avoid clobbering concurrent updates. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
